clue.text: Charm overturning plot with desire

indicators.note: overturning turns the synonym for plot round so it is read backwards

parts.note: a plot or intrigue can be called a web, as in a web of deceit
an itch is a restless desire or craving

explanation.surface: A spell that upsets a scheme while feeding a yearning.
explanation.walkthrough: 'plot' reads as a garden bed or a scheme; here it is a web of intrigue, and 'overturning' turns it end to end.
explanation.definitionFit: To charm someone is to enchant or captivate them, a synonym.

clue.text: See 18
Why we mean, athletic cheats will pay for dalliance?

definitions.text: Why we mean, athletic cheats will pay for dalliance?

indicators.note: dalliance means playing about, signalling that the letters play about into a new order

explanation.surface: A complaint that sporting cheats should be punished for messing about.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for dalliance' rearranges all thirty letters of WHY WE MEAN ATHLETIC CHEATS WILL PAY into the proverb.
explanation.definitionFit: The proverb says that people misbehave and fool about when nobody in authority is watching.

clue.text: TV quiz required its opening …

definitions.meaning: ... is a British colloquial name for television
on the old British game show Take Your Pick

explanation.surface: A television game show demanded a lid be lifted.
explanation.definitionFit: Television is called the box in casual British speech, and a quiz show famously had contestants open one.

clue.text: … its closure may reveal its location

definitions.text: … its closure may reveal its location

parts.words: its closure may reveal its location
parts.note: the closure of the word box is its last letter X, and X marks the spot where buried riches lie on a pirate map

explanation.surface: Shutting a lid could show where something lies.
explanation.walkthrough: Continuing from 3-down, the end of BOX is X, as in 'X marks the spot'.
explanation.definitionFit: Buried riches whose spot is traditionally shown by an X on a map.

clue.text: Sea dweller taking sides about 50% cut in medical branch

indicators.note: about means the pair of side letters goes round the trimmed branch of medicine

parts.note: left and right sides give L and R

indicators.note: cutting fifty per cent removes the back half of the ten-letter branch of medicine

parts.note: obstetrics is the branch of medicine dealing with childbirth

explanation.surface: A creature of the sea is somehow caught up in a hospital department's budget cuts.
explanation.walkthrough: '50% cut' halves OBSTETRICS to OBSTE, and 'about' puts L and R round it.
explanation.definitionFit: A lobster is a large marine crustacean, an example of a creature living in the sea.

clue.text: Eco-friendly motorist thus fared badly entering shelter

indicators.note: entering means the scrambled letters go inside the word for shelter

parts.note: lee is the sheltered side, away from the wind

indicators.note: badly suggests the letters of fared come out wrong and rearranged

explanation.surface: A green driver had a rough time finding cover.
explanation.walkthrough: 'motorist thus' makes the definition describe a driver who uses unleaded petrol; 'badly' signals the anagram and 'entering' the container.
explanation.definitionFit: A motorist using unleaded petrol drives in a way that is free of lead, kinder to the environment.

clue.text: Here view the latest part of round motors

parts.note: a bullet is part of a round of ammunition
inboards are boat motors mounted inside the hull

explanation.surface: Instructions to see the newest part of a race of cars.
explanation.walkthrough: 'round' suggests a lap or circuit but is ammunition; 'motors' are inboard engines on boats.
explanation.definitionFit: A noticeboard on which current news is posted for people to read.

clue.text: See 2
Spits in this revolutionary eating place

definitions.text: Spits in this revolutionary eating place

parts.words: Spits in this revolutionary eating place
parts.note: the spits are roasting skewers that turn round, revolutionary in the literal sense, in a restaurant serving roast meat

explanation.surface: Someone spits in a radical restaurant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spits' looks like a verb and 'revolutionary' like politics, but they are rotating skewers.
explanation.definitionFit: A restaurant or appliance where meat roasts on turning spits.

clue.text: Female flying on the previous day

parts.note: re means on or concerning, as in business letters
the eve is the day before an event

explanation.surface: A woman takes off the day before.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Female flying' means a female bird: the reeve is the female of the ruff, a wading bird.
explanation.definitionFit: The reeve is the name given to the hen of the ruff, a bird, so a flying female.

clue.text: As a result of which least died horribly? No!

definitions.text: As a result of which least died horribly? No!

indicators.note: horribly suggests the letters of least died are mangled into a new order

explanation.surface: A grim question about a catastrophe, answered with a flat denial.
explanation.walkthrough: The rearranged letters give a word meaning that the most died, which is why the clue's question gets its 'No!'.
explanation.definitionFit: Something deadliest causes the most deaths, the opposite of the fewest dying.

clue.text: Heath Robinson, or Heath-Robinson? This makes it the latter!

definitions.text: Heath Robinson, or Heath-Robinson? This makes it the latter!

parts.words: Heath Robinson, or Heath-Robinson? This makes it the latter!
parts.note: a stroke is a printed dash or hyphen; adding one to the cartoonist's name turns it into the adjective, and the cartoonist himself was an inventive genius of absurd gadgets

explanation.surface: A puzzle about the difference between a man's name and the adjective formed from it.
explanation.walkthrough: W. Heath Robinson was a British cartoonist famous for drawing absurdly elaborate machines; 'Heath-Robinson' with a hyphen means ingeniously makeshift.
explanation.definitionFit: A brilliant inspired idea, here also read literally as a stroke (hyphen) on a genius's name.

clue.text: Cheat pro with admission of Germany victory

indicators.note: admission means letting in, so the other pieces are let into the word for pro

parts.note: a pro is slang for a prostitute, as is hooker
D is the international vehicle registration for Germany
a win is a victory

explanation.surface: A cheating professional lets Germany win.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pro' looks like a professional but is slang for a prostitute; 'with admission of' lets the German vehicle code and the victory in.
explanation.definitionFit: A deceiver who tricks people is one who hoodwinks, a synonym for cheat.

clue.text: One affording basic protection from water throughout Oxford?

definitions.text: One affording basic protection from water

parts.note: over can mean throughout, as in all over the place
an Oxford is a style of laced shoe

explanation.surface: Something that keeps the whole of Oxford dry.
explanation.walkthrough: Oxford looks like the city but is a type of shoe; 'basic' means at the base, on the feet.
explanation.definitionFit: A waterproof cover worn over ordinary footwear protects the feet, the lowest part, from wet.

clue.text: Dog keeps energy in for mauling

indicators.note: mauling suggests the letters are torn about and rearranged

parts.note: E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: A dog keeps its energy up for a good savaging.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for mauling' rearranges KEEPS, E and IN.
explanation.definitionFit: The Pekinese is a small long-haired breed of dog originally from China.

clue.text: Significant outbreak of flu follows uprising of old domestics

indicators.note: follows means the scrambled flu comes after the reversed slaves
uprising in a down clue means the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: esnes were domestic slaves in Anglo-Saxon England

indicators.note: an outbreak scatters the letters of flu into a new order

explanation.surface: A flu epidemic follows a revolt by servants of old.
explanation.walkthrough: 'uprising of' turns ESNES up to SENSE, and 'outbreak of' makes FUL from FLU.
explanation.definitionFit: Something full of meaning is significant, a rare synonym.

clue.text: See 4
One leading following across Red Sea? Ludicrous, we won't hear of it!

indicators.note: across means the pair of letters lies across the middle of the scrambled sea's name
ludicrous suggests the letters of Red Sea are absurdly jumbled
leading means the letter from one comes in front of the letter for following

parts.note: one can be A, the indefinite article
F is the standard abbreviation for following, as in page references

explanation.surface: A leader of the Israelites crossing the Red Sea is dismissed as absurd, a story some refuse to hear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One leading' across the Red Sea suggests Moses, but it is just A put before F; 'Ludicrous' scrambles the sea and 'across' places the pair in its middle.
explanation.definitionFit: Words that fall on deaf ears go unheeded, the idiom behind refusing to hear something.

clue.text: Skirt courts carriers of hotel drinks

parts.note: a mini is a short skirt
the bar is a court of law, so courts can be bars

explanation.surface: A woman in a short skirt goes out with someone who serves cocktails in hotels.
explanation.definitionFit: Hotel rooms hold small fridges stocked with drinks, which carry them for guests.

clue.text: Excess that is working up muscles

parts.note: a glut is an excess or surplus

indicators.note: working up in a down clue reads the letters from bottom to top

parts.note: ie is the abbreviation of id est, that is

explanation.surface: Too much effort building up muscles.
explanation.walkthrough: 'working up' is the reversal signal, natural in a down clue; the plural of gluteus ends in I.
explanation.definitionFit: The gluteal muscles of the buttocks, plural of gluteus.

clue.text: See 6
What the king of Blefuscu said upon bumping into the king of Lilliput?

definitions.text: What the king of Blefuscu said upon bumping into the king of Lilliput?

parts.words: What the king of Blefuscu said upon bumping into the king of Lilliput?
parts.note: Blefuscu and Lilliput are the tiny kingdoms in Gulliver's Travels, so the remark one king might make on meeting another is the stock phrase for an unexpected encounter, taken literally about a miniature world

explanation.surface: Two rulers from Swift's satire meet by chance.
explanation.walkthrough: The everyday phrase said on a chance meeting fits the literal world of six-inch people.
explanation.definitionFit: The expression said when meeting someone unexpectedly, here literally true of tiny Lilliputians.

clue.text: See 13
Gooseberry's offspring? Result of one getting together with partner cut short sport in outfit

indicators.note: in means the run of pieces is placed inside the word for outfit

parts.note: a kit is a set of sports clothing
one is the Roman numeral I

indicators.note: cut short drops the final letter of the word for partner

parts.note: a wife is a marriage partner
RU is rugby union

explanation.surface: A gooseberry fathering something, and a sportsman marrying and getting kitted out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cut short' trims WIFE to WIF. This fruit was once sold as the Chinese gooseberry, hence its 'offspring'.
explanation.definitionFit: This fruit was formerly called the Chinese gooseberry, so it is whimsically its descendant.

clue.text: Mischievous chap partially responsible for Piper Alpha

indicators.note: partially means only part of the words Piper Alpha supply the letters

explanation.surface: Someone blamed in part for the Piper Alpha disaster.
explanation.walkthrough: Piper Alpha was a North Sea oil platform destroyed by fire in 1988.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a boy's name, so any chap may bear it; the mischief is surface colour.

clue.text: Our number one's own number one?

definitions.text: Our number one's own number one?

parts.words: Our number one's own number one?
parts.note: our number one is the monarch, and number one is slang for oneself, so this is how a king or queen says I

explanation.surface: A question about what matters most to our leader.
explanation.walkthrough: A monarch traditionally refers to himself or herself as 'we'.
explanation.definitionFit: The plural pronoun used by a sovereign in place of I, the ruler's own word for self.

clue.text: Where to seek sounder French article with panache

parts.note: a sounder is a herd of wild pigs, which you would look for in a sty
le is the French masculine definite article

explanation.surface: Someone looks for a better French article with flair.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sounder' looks like a comparative of sound but is a herd of swine.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something stylishly or with flair is doing it with panache, an idiom.
